summary_plain: Moves about 40 arcseconds per hour across 24 images over 13.0 hours. It matches the known asteroid 295 Theresia (A890 QA).

orbit.reported_orbit: The arc is too short to fix one orbit, so this is the most circular of the 860 sampled orbits that fit the detections; the clones show the range.

known_object.observer: SPHEREx (geocentric JPL predictions corrected with the spacecraft position from the FITS headers)

scores.definition: Rule-based ranking score in [0, 1]: motion_consistency x snr x (1 - artifact_likelihood). It orders candidates for review. It is not a probability.

explanation.text: Detected in 24 SPHEREx exposures spanning 13.0 hours. It moves 40.1 arcseconds per hour toward position angle 65 degrees. A straight-line motion plus orbital-parallax fit leaves 0.46 arcseconds of scatter. SPHEREx's own orbital parallax puts it roughly 2.41 AU away (range 1.57 to 5.22 AU). Its faintest detection has a signal-to-noise ratio of 19.7. Its positions match JPL's prediction for 295 Theresia (A890 QA) to within 0.7 arcseconds at every epoch.
